stages.title: FEDERAL TEST, FORMATION AND TERRITORY

groups.heading: FEDERAL TEST
items: Constitution protects Union and State authority in assigned spheres.
Both levels act directly on citizens; neither is an ordinary delegate.

groups.heading: FORMATION
items: India is a holding-together federation with a strong Union.
Union of States is not a compact among sovereign States.

groups.heading: TERRITORY
items: Article 3 requires presidential recommendation and State views, not State consent.
Reorganisation law is outside Article 368 under Article 4.

stages.answer_line: Federalism joins constitutionally protected regional autonomy to shared rule within one sovereign order.

stages.title: FEDERAL FEATURES AND UNION BIAS

groups.heading: FEDERAL
items: Written supreme Constitution, divided power, selective rigidity and courts.
State competence is autonomous but not sovereign.

groups.heading: UNION BIAS
items: Residuary power, State-field exceptions, emergencies and fiscal capacity.
Single citizenship, integrated services and centrally appointed Governor.

groups.heading: VERDICT
items: Centralising powers are constitutional and reviewable.
S.R. Bommai (1994) prevents Union bias from extinguishing federalism.

stages.answer_line: India is constitutionally federal and Union-weighted; “quasi-federal” is analysis, not constitutional text.

stages.title: LEGISLATIVE DISTRIBUTION AND CONFLICT

groups.heading: ALLOCATION
items: Article 246 orders the three Lists; Article 246A separately structures GST.
Article 248 and Union Entry 97 vest residuary power in Parliament.

groups.heading: DOCTRINES
items: Pith and substance tests true nature; harmonious construction reconciles.
Territorial nexus and colourable legislation police limits.

groups.heading: REPUGNANCY
items: Article 254 principally concerns Concurrent List conflict.
Presidential assent can save a State law locally; Parliament may later override.

stages.answer_line: Legislative federalism first characterises and reconciles overlap, then applies supremacy only to irreconcilable conflict.
source_references: notes\Final-Learning-Packages\_deep-content-review\reviews\polity-12\g3-source\polity-12_g3-reviewed-source.md#05. Legislative distribution: Articles 245-255 and the Seventh Schedule

stages.title: PARLIAMENT ENTERING THE STATE FIELD

groups.heading: TRIGGERS
items: 249: Rajya Sabha national-interest resolution; 250: national emergency.
252: two or more States request; 253: treaty implementation.

groups.heading: DURATION
items: 249/250 laws survive six months after authority ends.
Article 252 laws apply to requesting/adopting States and Parliament controls repeal.

groups.heading: LIMIT
items: Each route has a separate trigger and scope.
Exceptional access does not permanently erase List II.

stages.answer_line: Parliament enters List II through enumerated constitutional doors, not a general supremacy clause.
source_references: notes\Final-Learning-Packages\_deep-content-review\reviews\polity-12\g3-source\polity-12_g3-reviewed-source.md#06. When Parliament may legislate on the State List

stages.title: ADMINISTRATIVE RELATIONS: DIRECTIONS, DELEGATION, COUNCILS

groups.heading: COMPLIANCE
items: Articles 256-257 secure law compliance and prevent impedance of Union power.
Directions are text-bounded, not a general administrative takeover.

groups.heading: DELEGATION
items: 258 entrusts Union functions to States with consent.
258A permits State-to-Union entrustment with Union consent.

groups.heading: LEGAL SPACE
items: 261 gives full faith and credit.
262 needs parliamentary law for water adjudication/exclusion; 263 enables ISC.

stages.answer_line: Administrative federalism combines bounded directions with reciprocal delegation and consultative dispute management.
source_references: notes\Final-Learning-Packages\_deep-content-review\reviews\polity-12\g3-source\polity-12_g3-reviewed-source.md#07. Administrative and financial distribution: the missing operational bridge

stages.title: FINANCIAL DISTRIBUTION AND FISCAL AUTONOMY

groups.heading: REVENUE
items: 268/269/269A assign levy, collection and apportionment.
270 structures the divisible pool; 275 and 282 are distinct grant routes.

groups.heading: INSTITUTIONS
items: 280-281 create Finance Commission reporting.
16th FC report: 17 Nov 2025; 41% vertical share for 2026-31.

groups.heading: FRICTION
items: 293 may condition State borrowing consent.
Cesses, schemes and unequal capacity can narrow effective autonomy.

stages.answer_line: Fiscal federalism converts formal List II authority into usable capacity through assignment, devolution, grants and bargaining.

stages.title: BASIC STRUCTURE, ARTICLE 355 AND PRESIDENT’S RULE

groups.heading: CASE CHAIN
items: State of West Bengal v. Union of India (1962) rejects sovereign-State compact theory.
Kesavananda Bharati (1973) limits amendment; S.R. Bommai (1994) names federalism Basic Structure.

groups.heading: DUTY / REMEDY
items: Article 355 creates a Union duty, not automatic Article 356 authority.
356 requires constitutional breakdown; 357 handles legislative power.

groups.heading: CONTROL
items: Proclamations are reviewable; restoration is possible.
Disputed majority ordinarily belongs on the House floor.

stages.answer_line: Article 355 states responsibility; Article 356 is an exceptional, reviewable remedy rather than its automatic consequence.

stages.title: WORKING MODES AND SHARED-RULE INSTITUTIONS

groups.heading: MODES
items: Cooperation coordinates; competition innovates; bargaining negotiates.
Confrontation can remain constitutional through courts and politics.

groups.heading: INSTITUTIONS
items: Rajya Sabha, ISC, Zonal Councils, GST Council and Finance Commission.
NITI, All-India Services and courts connect policy and implementation.

groups.heading: LIMIT
items: Non-binding consultation is not irrelevant.
Mohit Minerals (2022) preserves legislative autonomy within GST dialogue.

stages.answer_line: Healthy federalism converts inevitable conflict into reasons, negotiation, adjudication and electoral accountability.

stages.title: ASYMMETRIC FEDERALISM AS ACCOMMODATION

groups.heading: DESIGN
items: Different units may receive different constitutional arrangements.
Asymmetry accommodates history, identity, land and administration.

groups.heading: FORMS
items: Fifth Schedule uses Governor/TAC protective administration.
Sixth Schedule uses autonomous district/regional councils.

groups.heading: LIMIT
items: Post-2019 J&K must be stated through current law.
Asymmetry needs constitutional purpose; it is not arbitrary inequality.

stages.answer_line: Asymmetry can strengthen integration by protecting difference inside common citizenship.

stages.title: REPRESENTATION AND CURRENT FEDERAL FRICTION

groups.heading: REPRESENTATION
items: Rajya Sabha seats are unequal; Lok Sabha allocation shapes federal weight.
The 131st Bill was negatived 17 Apr 2026; its 850 ceiling is not law.

groups.heading: STATUS LIMITS
items: Census conduct/reference dates are not publication or delimitation dates.
No State-wise seat or women-reservation election date may be forecast.

groups.heading: FRICTIONS
items: Governor: no fixed timeline/deemed assent; unexplained inaction remains reviewable.
The 2024 West Bengal ruling decided Article 131 maintainability, not all CBI merits.

stages.answer_line: Current federal claims must separate enacted law, defeated proposals, notified processes and speculative outcomes.

stages.title: TEN VERIFIED PYQ ROUTES AND PRELIMS TRAPS

groups.heading: PYQ MAP
items: 2020 modes/centralisation; 2021 CBI; 2022 parties.
2023 Article 356/GST; 2024 trust; 2025 fiscal federalism.

groups.heading: PRELIMS
items: Independent judiciary indicates federal character.
Prisons are List II; colonial administration is not the constitutional reason.

groups.heading: TRAPS
items: Article 254 is Concurrent-specific; 262 exclusion requires law.
Article 355 is not automatic 356; GST advice is not binding.

stages.answer_line: A high-scoring federal answer pairs every broad label with an Article, institution, case and limitation.

stages.title: MARKS-SCALED ANSWER SPINE AND QUALIFIED VERDICT

groups.heading: 10 MARKS
items: Define the federal test; use one Article cluster and one case.
Answer the directive in about 150 words.

groups.heading: 15 MARKS
items: Add legislative, administrative and fiscal mechanisms.
Use named evidence, counterpoint and specific reform.

groups.heading: 20 MARKS
items: Integrate asymmetry, representation and current status.
End with a graded Union-capacity/State-autonomy verdict.

stages.mechanism_strip: Move from definition to distribution, operation, evidence, limitation, reform and a graded verdict.
stages.answer_line: India’s federal legitimacy depends on converting superior Union capacity into consultation, equalisation and constitutional restraint.

groups.heading: LABELS
items: Wheare: quasi-federal; Austin: cooperative; Morris-Jones: bargaining.
Jennings, Appleby and sui generis labels widen evaluation.

groups.heading: DISCIPLINE
items: No label replaces Articles, institutions or cases.
Use scholarship only after the complete Core route.
